solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Creature that flies past insect swatter, sometimes? (7,3)

indicators.note: one thing that has gone past another is now behind it, so the flier is written after the insect

blocks.note: a chirping insect of the grasshopper family
the flying mammal

annotation.surface: A flying creature zips past someone waving an insect swatter.
annotation.walkthrough: The swatter looks like the thing that kills insects, but it is the insect's name that begins the answer. Cricket is the English bat-and-ball game.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by function: the batsman swats the ball away with it, and the question mark admits that is only one way to see the job.

entries.clue: Old country I adore has less heart for revolution? (8)

indicators.note: a word with less heart has lost its middle, so HAS drops its central A
letters sent for revolution are overturned and come back in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
HAS minus its middle letter A

annotation.surface: Someone adores an old country that has lost its spirit for revolution.
annotation.walkthrough: Rhodesia was the former name of Zimbabwe. 'Revolution' fits the history of old countries, which is what hides its job of stirring the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A historical name: the country became Zimbabwe in 1980, so the name now belongs to the past.

entries.clue: I’m surprised by report of revolting action (3)

indicators.note: a report is a sound that is heard, so the word wanted is one that sounds like the next idea

blocks.note: a British exclamation of mild astonishment
a revolting action is a coup, a sudden seizure of power by rebels; said aloud, its P is silent

annotation.surface: Someone is shocked by news of a revolting deed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Revolting' reads as disgusting, but here it means rising in revolt: a coup, which sounds exactly like the exclamation coo!
annotation.definitionFit: An interjection: the dated British 'Coo!' is what one says for 'I'm surprised'.

entries.clue: Dark wood inlay in marquetry no better when raised (5)

indicators.note: an inlay is set into a surface, so the answer is set into the run of words that follow
in a down clue, raising letters lifts the last to the top, so they read bottom to top

blocks.note: the letters run across marquetrY NO BEtter

annotation.surface: A craftsman says a dark wood inlay in marquetry is no improvement once raised.
annotation.walkthrough: Inlay really is how marquetry works, so the word sits in the surface as plain craft talk while it tells you the answer is set into the words.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain description: the heartwood of this tropical tree is nearly black and prized by cabinetmakers.

entries.clue: Having drunk large amount, upset facile jerk (7)

indicators.note: something that has drunk a thing holds it inside, so one piece swallows another
to upset is to overturn, and in a down clue an overturned word reads upwards

blocks.note: glib = facile, then turned over to BILG
a ton = a large amount, as in tons of money

annotation.surface: After a big drinking session, someone knocks over a smooth-talking idiot.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Jerk' looks like an insult, but it is the dried meat, as in beef jerky. Biltong is the South African version.
annotation.definitionFit: Near-synonym from another cuisine: both are strips of salted, air-dried meat, one American, one South African.

entries.clue: Small white crystals at best, all shaken (5,4)

indicators.note: letters that are shaken tumble out of their order, as salt does from a shaker

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

annotation.surface: Small white crystals come out best when everything is given a shake.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shaken' belongs to the picture, since salt comes out of a shaker, so it passes as description rather than an instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by appearance: sodium chloride for the dinner table comes as tiny white cubes.

entries.clue: Information in more than one novel? (4)

blocks.note: facts about what has just happened
novel as the adjective meaning fresh, made plural as if it were a noun

annotation.surface: A reader finds information spread across several novels.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Novel' reads as a book but is the adjective new; the question mark admits that pluralising an adjective to get NEWS is a joke.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the first half; the second is a crossword-only sense, new plus a plural S.

entries.clue: Very close, scrawny couple? (4,3,4)

blocks.note: level in a race, as horses are when neither head is in front
a pair so thin they seem to be nothing but throat, side by side

annotation.surface: A thin pair of people stand very close together.
annotation.walkthrough: The second half is whimsical: a couple so scrawny there is nothing to either of them but neck. The question mark flags the stretch.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom from horse racing, where a close finish is judged by whose neck is in front.

entries.clue: Petite dish in Love Story, say (6)

blocks.note: wee = small (Scots)
a baked dish with a pastry crust

annotation.surface: A small plate of food features in a romantic tale.
annotation.walkthrough: Love Story is a 1970 tearjerker film, so 'say' marks it as an example of the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the 1970 film is the classic sentimental tearjerker.

entries.clue: Procedure or boring work that keeps estate operating smoothly? (5,3)

indicators.note: a drill boring into wood goes inside it, so one piece bores into another

blocks.note: MO = modus operandi, a way of doing things
toil = hard work
taken as written, set inside TOIL

annotation.surface: A dull routine keeps a country estate running without a hitch.
annotation.walkthrough: The estate is not land with a big house but an estate car, the British name for a station wagon. 'Or' is part of the wordplay, not a choice between two things.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by function: an estate is a car, and the lubricant in its engine is what lets it run smoothly.

entries.clue: Champion, one retiring? (6)

blocks.note: read as a noun: someone who stands up for a cause
retiring in its literal sense of withdrawing, so someone moving in reverse

annotation.surface: A title-holder decides to retire.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Champion' suggests a winner, but it means a supporter. 'Retiring' reads as shy or leaving work, yet it is literal retreat.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses of one verb: to back a cause is to champion it, and to back away is to retire.

entries.clue: Lower garment (6)

blocks.note: read as low-er, something that lows or moos: a cow from a Channel Island breed
a knitted top, pullover or sweater

annotation.surface: Something to wear on the bottom half.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lower garment' reads as trousers, the opposite of upper. Split it: a lower is an animal that lows, and the Jersey cow is one.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic-only sense, a cow as one who lows, joined to a plain synonym for a sweater.

entries.clue: Stew low on calories — get it! (3,3,5)

blocks.note: to stew is to fume quietly
as in light beer or light mayonnaise

annotation.surface: A diet stew recipe is recommended with enthusiasm.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stew' looks like food, which the calories encourage, but it means to fume.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom for sudden understanding, as a convert does, matching the exasperated 'get it!'

entries.clue: Musical device used in bar to keep time (8)

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so the outer piece holds the inner one

blocks.note: an optic is the measuring device on an upside-down spirit bottle in a British bar
an era is a period of time

annotation.surface: A musician's gadget, like a metronome, helps keep time in each bar.
annotation.walkthrough: The bar is not a bar of music but a pub counter, and the device is an optic. 'Keep time' reads as one musical phrase, but the words split.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose adjective match: anything belonging to opera is musical, though not everything musical is opera.

entries.clue: Writer’s drawn on amendment to legal document (5,7)

indicators.note: in an across clue, a piece placed on another follows it, so the second half is written after the first

blocks.note: a rider is a clause added to a bill or contract
drawn = gaunt and tired-looking

annotation.surface: An author has sketched something onto a change to a contract.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drawn' suggests sketching, but it is the look of a tired face. H. Rider Haggard wrote King Solomon's Mines.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: the Victorian novelist behind She and King Solomon's Mines.

entries.clue: Shower of pellets also hit various soldiers (9)

indicators.note: letters made various take on different forms, so they come out in another order

blocks.note: the letters of ALSO HIT, rearranged
RM = Royal Marines

annotation.surface: Soldiers are peppered with pellets and hit as well.
annotation.walkthrough: The pellets sound like gunfire, fitting the soldiers, but they are balls of ice.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain description: ice pellets falling from the sky in a burst.

entries.clue: County councillor accepting nothing new disheartened everybody (8)

indicators.note: one who accepts a thing takes it in, so the abbreviation takes the next letter inside
a word that loses heart loses its middle, so WE ALL drops its central E

blocks.note: Cr is the abbreviation for councillor
O = zero, nothing
N = new
WE ALL, everybody, loses its middle letter E

annotation.surface: A county councillor backs nothing new and everyone is dispirited.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Disheartened' reads as dispirited, but it cuts the middle out of WE ALL.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: the county at England's south-western tip.

entries.clue: Bloody Mary perhaps in fur coat? (4,2,3,3)

blocks.note: the vodka and tomato cocktail, a classic morning-after cure
what a hound's coat is made of

annotation.surface: A queen or a cocktail turns up wrapped in fur.
annotation.walkthrough: Bloody Mary could be Mary I of England, but it is the cocktail. 'Perhaps' marks it as one example.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom by example: a drink taken to ease a hangover, from the old belief that the bite is cured by the biter.

entries.clue: Pole owns home rated as inadequate? (3-4)

indicators.note: what a thing owns it holds, so the pole holds the home inside it

blocks.note: an oar is a pole for rowing
a nest is a bird's home

annotation.surface: A Polish homeowner's house has been given a poor rating.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital P makes Pole look like a Polish person, but it is a long stick. The question mark allows that the lowest rating is not always a failure.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by consequence: the lowest mark on a hotel or review scale suggests something not good enough.

entries.clue: Personalised work of art, garbage I might add (6)

blocks.note: tat = cheap tacky rubbish (British)
too = as well, what you say when adding something

annotation.surface: A critic dismisses a bespoke artwork as rubbish, and says so openly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Personalised' is literal: the artwork is drawn on the person.
annotation.definitionFit: A playful definition: ink art made on one body is personal in the most literal way.

entries.clue: Cotton on wheels in English city (8)

indicators.note: in an across clue, a piece placed on another follows it, so the thread is written after the vehicle

blocks.note: wheels is slang for a vehicle
lisle is a fine, strong cotton thread

annotation.surface: Cotton is carted about on wheels in a city.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cotton on' tempts as the phrase meaning understand; here the words work separately.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: the cathedral city in Cumbria, close to the Scottish border.

entries.clue: Major league has defended blood sport (6)

indicators.note: a defender surrounds what it protects, so the outer word wraps round the inner one

blocks.note: the big league is the major league
blood = family, as in blood relatives

annotation.surface: A top sports league has stood up for a cruel pastime.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Blood sport' reads as hunting, but blood is family and the sport stands alone.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: cycling is a competitive sport.

entries.clue: American flag hoisted in wood (5)

indicators.note: a hoisted flag goes up the pole, and in a down clue going up means reading bottom to top

blocks.note: A = American
a flag, or flagstone, is a paving slab

annotation.surface: The Stars and Stripes is run up a pole in a forest.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flag' and 'hoisted' look like one picture of a banner going up, but the flag is a paving stone.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: the very light timber used for model aircraft.

entries.clue: Party with hoofing? (4,2)

blocks.note: any celebration; together with the rest it reads as a dance
hoofing is slang for dancing, but read it as an animal with hooves throwing the party

annotation.walkthrough: 'Hoofing' means dancing, which fits any party, but a male deer has hooves, so this is the deer's party: the British bachelor party.
annotation.definitionFit: A pun on the name: the pre-wedding night out is named after a male deer, a hoofed animal.

entries.clue: Message shortening lease is returned (8)

indicators.note: something returned is sent back the way it came, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: shortening is baking fat, and marge is British slang for margarine
to lease a property is to let it

annotation.surface: A notice says a tenancy is being cut short and handed back.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shortening' reads as cutting the lease down, but it is the cooking fat.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: a wired message, once delivered printed on a slip.

entries.clue: Letter in my word! (3)

blocks.note: the seventh letter, spelt out as a word
an exclamation of surprise, mainly American

annotation.surface: Someone spots a letter in something they have said.
annotation.walkthrough: 'My word' looks like a word belonging to me; it is the exclamation.
annotation.definitionFit: A spelt-out letter name, joined to an interjection that means the same as 'my word!'

entries.clue: Alcoholic drink: too much to pass to the left? (4)

blocks.note: a fortified wine from the Douro valley
surface padding, painting a greedy guest at the dinner table
the sailor's word for the left-hand side of a ship

annotation.surface: At dinner a guest has had too much of the drink that goes round the table.
annotation.walkthrough: By tradition the decanter of this wine is passed to the left round a dinner table, and the same word is the sailor's left.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses of one word: a fortified wine and the nautical left side.

entries.clue: Bit into unfinished cherry, a meaty thing (10)

indicators.note: one piece goes into another, so the small word sits inside the cherry
a word left unfinished stops short of its last letter, so MORELLO loses its O

blocks.note: a morello is a sour cherry; drop the last letter O
a tad = a bit
taken as written

annotation.surface: Someone bites into a half-eaten cherry and finds it oddly meaty.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bit' reads as the past of bite, which suits the cherry, but it is a small amount.
annotation.definitionFit: A vague definition by class: this large Bologna pork sausage is certainly meaty.
